# What does this data represent?

.pull-left4[

```{r echo = FALSE}
part1 <- circle[1:12, ]
part2 <- circle[13:24, ]

combined <- cbind(part1, part2)

kable(combined, format = "html", 
      col.names = c("x", "y", "x", "y"))
```


]

# Gestalt Psychology

.pull-left4[

<ul>
  <li class="m1"><span><high>reification</high></span></li>
<ul>
  <li>  experience more spatial information than is present</li>
</ul>
  <li class="m2"><span>emergence<high></high> </span></li>
<ul>
  <li> do not recognize componente (head, tail ...) </li>
</ul>
  <li class="m3"><span>Prägnanz (simplicity) <high><high></span></li>
  
  
</ul>

]

.pull-right5[

</center>
]

.pull-right5[

```{r echo = FALSE, fig.wdth=5, fig.height=5}
mtcars <- mtcars %>%
  mutate(model=rownames(mtcars))

mtcars$model2<-factor(as.character(mtcars$model))
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=mpg, y=model2)) + 
  geom_point(color="black") + 
  theme_bw() + ylab(NULL)
```


]

# Law of ...

</ul>

]

.pull-right5[

```{r echo = FALSE, fig.wdth=5, fig.height=5}
# Make number of cylinders a factor, so ggplot will choose a discrete scale.
mtcars$cyl<-factor(mtcars$cyl)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color=cyl), size = 5) + 
  xlab("weight (1,000 lbs)") +
  scale_color_brewer("Cylinders", type="qual", palette=1) +
  theme_bw()
```


]

```{r echo = FALSE, fig.wdth=5, fig.height=5}
  geom_line() + 
  geom_point() + 
  expand_limits(y=0) +
  scale_y_continuous("Count") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Give focus

.pull-left3[
<ul>
  <li class="m1"><span>Use <high>few colors</high> and use them <high>strategically</high> (applies also to contrast).</span></li>
  <br>
  <li class="m2"><span>Choose colors that are <high>appropriate</high> and <high>pleasing</high>.</span></li>
  <ul class="level">
    <li><span>Tools: <a href="https://color.adobe.com/de/create">color.adobe.com</a> oder <a href="https://coolors.co/">coolors.co</a></span></li>
    <li><span>Farbsätze: <a href="https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/viridis/vignettes/intro-to-viridis.html">viridis</a></span></li>
  </ul>
  <br>
  <li class="m3"><span>Be <high>consistent</high>.</span></li>
</ul>

]

</ul>

# Tables

.pull-left3[

<ul>
  <li class="m1"><span>Are <high>precise</high> and complete.</span></li>
  <li class="m2"><span>Are <high>processed serially</high> and need time.</span></li>
  <li class="m3"><span><high>Decluttered tables</high> are easier to read.</span></li>
  <li class="m4"><span><high>Colors</high> can help with giving focus.</span></li>
</ul>
]

</p>

]

---

# Charts

.pull-left3[

<ul>
  <li class="m1"><span>Are <high>processed in parallel</high>.</span></li>
  <li class="m2"><span>Are often <high>easier to understand</high> than tables.</span></li>
  <li class="m3"><span>Are often <high>more difficult to create</high> than tables.</span></li>
</ul>

]

]

# Annotation

.pull-left3[

<ul>
  <li class="m1"><span>Annotation is <high>very important</high></span></li>
  <li class="m2"><span>Always useful:</span></li>
  <ul class="level">
    <li><span>Axes titles</span></li>
  </ul>
  <br>
  <li class="m3"><span>Mostly useful:</span></li>
  <ul class="level">
    <li><span>Plot title</span></li>
  </ul>
  <br>
  <li class="m4"><span>Often useful:</span></li>
  <ul class="level">
    <li><span>Subtitle</span></li>
    <li><span>Legend</span></li>
    <li><span>Annotations in the plot</span></li>
  </ul>
</ul>

<h1>Pitches</h1>

# Pitches

.pull-left3[

<ul>
  <li class="m1"><span>Your <high>Sketch</high></span></li>
  <li class="m2"><span>2 slides - 2 Minutes</span></li>
  <li class="m3"><span>Discussion</span></li>
</ul>

]


.pull-right6[

In this session, you will introduce <high>your visualization sketch</high> to the rest of the group. 

You will have <high>2 slides and 2 minutes</high> for your pitch. 

Slide 1 should <high>only show a project title and an image</high> (e.g., from unsplash.com.) that helps you introduce and motivate your research question. 

Slide 2 should only show <high>your hand-drawn visualization sketch</high> and a slide title. No bullet points allowed. 

After each presentation there will be <high>3-5 minutes for peer feedback</high>, so please be prepared to comment on fellow participants’ presentations.

]
